title: Ir a...
goal: Talk about plans with ir a + infinitive, and give dates with months and seasons.

lessons.title: What are you going to do?
lessons.notes:
The easiest way to talk about the future is exactly like English 'going to': **ir + a + infinitive**.
**Voy a cocinar** (I'm going to cook) · **¿Vas a venir?** · **Vamos a viajar a México.**
Only ir changes; the second verb stays in the -ar / -er / -ir form.
**Hacer** (to do, to make) is the key verb for plans: **¿Qué vas a hacer?** (what are you going to do?).
Time words: **esta noche** (tonight), **esta tarde** (this afternoon), **este fin de semana**, **la próxima semana** (next week), **pronto** (soon). **Vamos a comer** can also mean 'let's eat!'.

lessons.title: Weekend plans
lessons.notes:
**¿Tienes planes para el sábado?** (got plans for Saturday?) - **No, nada especial.**
When you visit or see a **person**, Spanish adds a little **a** before them - the 'personal a': **Voy a visitar a mis abuelos.** Not for places: **Voy a visitar México.**
**El cumpleaños** (birthday) is literally 'completes-years'; it's the same in the plural: los cumpleaños.
A barbecue: **la barbacoa** is understood everywhere; Argentines have an **asado** and Mexicans **carne asada**.
**El partido** = the match, the game. **Pasear** = to go for a walk / stroll (**pasear al perro**).

lessons.title: The months
lessons.notes:
Months are written without a capital letter: **enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre**.
'In March' = **en marzo**.
Dates use plain numbers, with **el** and **de**: **el cinco de mayo** (the 5th of May) - no 'fifth'. The first of the month is often **el primero** in Latin America (**el primero de abril**), **el uno** in Spain.
The day comes before the month, as in Australia: 5/5 = el cinco de mayo. Setiembre is also spelt **setiembre** in some countries.

lessons.title: Seasons and dates
lessons.notes:
The seasons: **la primavera** (spring), **el verano** (summer), **el otoño** (autumn), **el invierno** (winter). 'In summer' = **en verano** or **en el verano**.
From Australia remember they're upside down for half the Spanish-speaking world: in Mexico and Spain **la Navidad** (Christmas) is in winter; in Argentina and Chile, as here, it's in summer.
Asking the date: **¿Qué fecha es hoy?** - **Hoy es el primero de abril.** Birthdays: **¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños?**
**El próximo año** (or **el año que viene**) = next year. **Las vacaciones** is always plural: holidays.

sentences.es: En Australia, la Navidad es en verano.
sentences.en: In Australia, Christmas is in summer.
accept_en: In Australia Christmas is in the summer.

sentences.es: El invierno es en junio, julio y agosto.
